title: Neuro Checks (Glasgow Coma Scale) Trend
scenario: A 52-year-old client is admitted to the neuro unit after a fall with a head injury. The nurse performs serial neurological checks over six hours.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: How should the nurse interpret the trend in the serial neurological assessments?

options.text: The client's neurological status is deteriorating
The client's neurological status is improving
The findings are stable and within normal limits
The changes reflect normal sleep and require no action

questions.rationale: The GCS falls from 15 to 8 with a newly dilated, sluggish right pupil, indicating a declining level of consciousness and rising intracranial pressure, not sleep or improvement.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Given the trend and the 04:00 findings, what is the nurse's priority action?

options.text: Notify the provider immediately of the deteriorating findings
Reassess the client at the next scheduled 06:00 check
Encourage the client to rest and dim the lights
Document the findings and continue routine monitoring

questions.rationale: A falling GCS with a newly dilated pupil signals possible herniation from rising intracranial pressure and is a neurological emergency; the nurse must notify the provider immediately rather than wait for the next check.
